# Mutants for the host-binding table (#00qn5az head 2)

Each mutant is one exact edit, run on Golem against the tests it names, then put back from a saved copy. The oracle rows run with `ADAMIC_GATE_UNCACHED=1`. The lower tests are in internal/lower/host_bindings_test.go, the audit in internal/load/host_bindings_test.go, and the oracle's in internal/oracle/host_bindings_test.go.

Adamic's isNodeLikeSystem mutant, `process` folded Absent turning isNodeLikeSystem's pin red, waits on Correctness's 99q amendment, which drops `typeof require` from it. While that test holds, isNodeLikeSystem is false on the oracle whatever `process` says, so the pin would be vacuous. Mutant (d) is its replacement on each row's own held-to-Node program, as Adamic moved it (Nov 6 00:27Z).

| Mutant | Edit | Red |
|---|---|---|
| (a) A read admitted with its guard removed | lower/host_bindings.go, `hostBindingDominated`: the final `return false` made `return true` | TestHostBindingReadsOutsideTheirGuardAreNotYet, all six rows: a guard bound to a local, a negated guard, an early return and the else branch of a test for "undefined" reach lowering and stop as the identifier's compiler-bug backstop ("a read of the host binding onProfilerEvent reached lowering"), `\|\|` stops as a BinaryExpression as a statement, and the guard in a called function as an optional call. None stops as the read it is. The oracle's TestHostBindingsAgreeWithNode stays green: its four programs read only under a guard |
| (b) A row's ruling dropped | internal/load/host_bindings.json, onProfilerEvent's `"ruling"` made `""` | TestHostBindingsAudit, at its first line: the table doesn't parse ("load: host binding row 1 (onProfilerEvent): no ruling or task names what made the row"). Every reader of the table fails closed with it, so ambientRefusal reports that error at the first ambient value declaration of any program |
| (c) The guard matched by name, not by symbol | lower/host_bindings.go, `hostBindingOf`: `row := l.hostBindingRow(symbol.Declarations[0])` made `row := named` | TestHostBindingShadowingLocalIsTheLocal, both rows: the parameter onProfilerEvent's guarded call lowers as the host binding's placeholder, and the local performance stops as the pending row. TestHostBindingsAgreeWithNode, shadow/main.ts, native, sanitized and javascript: they print "undefined" twice where Node prints "fired one", "function" and "undefined", the silent miscompile the symbol match stops. TestHostBindingWritesAreRefused's `globalThis['performance']` row goes red with them: its import of perf_hooks' performance now reads as the row |
| (d) `process` folded Absent | internal/load/host_bindings.json, process's native, javascript and wasm32 columns each made `{"answer": "Absent"}`, and its model's path `""` (a row with no Provided column names no model) | TestHostBindingsHeldToNode/process: each column says Absent where Node's typeof is "object", and the row, Absent on every target, now lowers, so native, sanitized and javascript print "undefined" where Node prints "object". TestHostBindingPendingRowsAreNotYet/process goes red with it: isNodeLikeSystem's `!process.browser` stops as an unguarded read of an Absent name instead of as the pending row, since the left of its `&&` is `typeof process !== "undefined" && !!process.nextTick`, not a guard alone |
| (e) Rule 50's receiver judged by its spelling | lower/host_bindings.go, `hostBindingGlobalThisRefusal`: `if !l.globalObject(receiver) && !l.globalObjectOperand(receiver) {` made `if !ast.IsIdentifier(receiver) \|\| receiver.Text() != "globalThis" {` | TestHostBindingWritesAreRefused, nine rows: a parameter of the global object's type, globalThis.globalThis, Node's global, the two unions and the intersection, the union and intersection parameters and the constrained type parameter, and TestGlobalObjectAsAReceiverIsAdmitted's write through global with them. Each stops elsewhere than rule 50's refusal: namespaceRefusal's not yet ("a namespace object used as a value"), or the global object as a value at a later node (the globalThis arm of the union, the cast's operand, the call that passes globalThis). The globalThis spelling's rows stay green. (Head 2 pinned an alias here; since head 3 an alias stops before, as the global object as a value, so a parameter typed typeof globalThis is the row that reaches rule 50 under another name) |
| (f) The receiver's type judged by its own symbol alone | lower/global_object.go, `globalObject`: `return global != nil && l.globalObjectType(l.checker.GetTypeAtLocation(node), global, map[*checker.Type]bool{})` made `return global != nil && l.checker.GetTypeAtLocation(node).Symbol() == global` | TestHostBindingWritesAreRefused, three rows: a parameter of a union with the global object and the type parameter constrained to it stop as namespaceRefusal's not yet, and a parameter of an intersection with it reaches the call that passes globalThis, two lines later. A union's and an intersection's symbol is nil and a type parameter's is its own, so none is the global object to that comparison. TestGlobalObjectAsAValueIsNotYet's Object.assign on globalThis goes red with them: its call's value, an intersection holding the global object, is no longer seen, so it stops at the argument instead. The expression forms, `(flag ? globalThis : other)` and `(globalThis as typeof globalThis & ...)`, stay green: globalObjectOperand finds the globalThis inside them |
| (g) The operands of the receiver not judged | lower/host_bindings.go, `hostBindingGlobalThisRefusal`: `if !l.globalObject(receiver) && !l.globalObjectOperand(receiver) {` made `if !l.globalObject(receiver) {` | TestHostBindingWritesAreRefused, the union the checker reduces to its other member: `(flag ? globalThis : other).process = other.process`, where other's type is a supertype of typeof globalThis, so the conditional's type is other's alone. Rule 50 lets it by, and it stops only as the global object as a value at its globalThis arm (head 2 alone: lowering's "reading process" at other's initializer, a line before) |
| (h) A widening to object admitted | lower/global_object.go, `globalObjectAdmitted`: `case ast.KindParenthesizedExpression:` made `case ast.KindParenthesizedExpression, ast.KindVariableDeclaration:`, so an initializer may take the global object | TestGlobalObjectAsAValueIsNotYet, nine rows. The object and empty-object views with Reflect.set, Object.assign and defineProperty carry the global object past the stop as an `object` and stop only on lowering's "reading globalThis", the Reflect.set road through. The Record and index-signature views fall back to the record view's not yet, and the alias's three rows stop a line later, at the call that takes the alias, no longer where the global object became a value |
| (i) No result of the global object judged | lower/global_object.go, `globalObjectResult`: `return global != nil && l.checker.IsTypeAssignableTo(l.checker.GetTypeOfSymbol(global), l.checker.GetTypeAtLocation(node))` made `return global != nil && false` | TestGlobalObjectAsAValueIsNotYet, the eight valueOf rows: Reflect.set on globalThis.valueOf() (Language's p01), and through globalThis.globalThis, an element-access callee, an optional call and valueOf of valueOf, stop as "a namespace member without a lowered binding"; Object.assign on it (p02) as Object.assign's shape stop; the widening to object (p08) as lowering's "reading globalThis"; and global.valueOf() (p04) as node:globals.global. None stops as the global object as a value, so lifting any of those would reopen Reflect.set's road |
